newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate sets debate on Mexico drugs issue.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate sets debate on Mexico drugs issue.

text.p: The U.S. Senate agreed on Thursday to open debate on compromise legislation chiding Mexico for its perceived failure to deal with the problem of illegal drugs flowing into the United States.
The legislation stops well short of overturning President Bill Clinton's finding that Mexico was cooperating fully in the anti-drug war.
The legislation, drafted by key senators in negotiations with administration officials, sets goals for intensifying the anti-drug fight.
Under a Senate agreement, the debate on the measure was due to last 4 hours and 45 minutes. It was expected to be approved by a wide majority later on Thursday.
The agreement for debate was reached after Republican Leader Trent Lott gave assurances that he would work to get a treaty banning chemical weapons to the Senate floor for action.
Democrats had threatened to hold up all Senate work to try to bring pressure on Republicans to set a date for debate on the treaty.
